messages:
vlad: heads-up — noticed recurring tail-latency blips in prod serving. nsys traces show repeated cudaMalloc (not CUDA kernel) stalls clustered around high-concurrency bursts. attaching quick notes :eyes:

maria: ugh, so not kernel time but allocator pauses? any correlation with batch size / KV cache churn?

vlad: yeah looks like spikes coincide with large KV cache fills and when we switch to cold model shards. example from the trace: CUDA API: cudaMalloc x24 at step 17-19, avg 2.9ms, outliers 45ms. kernel timeline clean otherwise.

alex: do we use cudaMallocAsync anywhere? I thought our pool switched to async allocator in the last runtime update.

vlad: runtime uses small arena + fallback to cudaMallocAsync for large blocks. but trace shows plain cudaMalloc (synchronous) calls — probably fallback path when pool is exhausted or when we request >arena_chunk_size.

kevin: can you paste the nsys invocation you used? i'll reproduce locally.

vlad: sure — command I used:
```
nsys profile --output=malloc_spike --trace=cuda,osrt,osrt_mem -f true --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi -- ./bin/redwood-server --config=config/prod.yaml --max-batch=32 --concurrency=48
```

jordan: quick checklist: 1) confirm arena reserve fraction, 2) check per-GPU arena fragmentation metric, 3) ensure cudaMallocAsync is enabled and actually used, 4) look for jemalloc/glibc malloc interplay on host side.

maria: i pulled the runtime metrics during that run. from telemetry: arena_reserved_frac=0.75, arena_used_peak=89%, fragmentation_est=0.21, fallback_malloc_calls=142. fragmentation > 0.2 is bad threshold for us.

sre-bot: note: alloc spikes also caused host OOM on one box yesterday — evicted one container. sending incident link: https://redwood/incidents/2026-03-malloc-oom

kevin: if fragmentation high, maybe our chunk size distribution is off. smaller long-lived KV caches create many small allocations, leaving holes. we could try switching to arena LIFO reuse and increase small-chunk slabing.

vlad: good point. i ran a small experiment toggling arena LIFO and increasing slab for 16KB/64KB classes. nsys sample results: fallback cudaMalloc dropped by ~70%, tail p99 latency improved from 210ms to 88ms on that micro-run.

alex: we should also evaluate cudaMallocAsync vs our pool. cudaMallocAsync reduces driver roundtrips only if blocks freed via cudaMemPoolFreeAsync; we need to ensure our free path goes through it. otherwise it still stalls.

maria: config snippet i propose to test in staging:
```
allocator.use_cudaMallocAsync=true
gpu.pool.reserve_frac=0.85
gpu.pool.slab_sizes=[16384,65536,262144]
gpu.pool.lifo_reuse=true
gpu.pool.release_threshold_ms=2000
```

vlad: +1 to that. also suggest enabling per-thread arenas to avoid cross-thread fragmentation in our serving threads. set arena.thread_local=true for the bench.

kevin: aside: we saw some allocation churn when switching model variants for fallback routing. maybe caching policy should pin KV cache shards for a short TTL to avoid repeated alloc/free cycles.

jordan: action items:
- kevin to run full 24hr staging run with the new pool slab config and lifo reuse (starts 03/18)
- vlad to instrument allocator to emit histograms for allocation sizes and number of fallback cudaMallocs per minute
- maria to test enabling cudaMallocAsync end-to-end and verify cudaMemPoolFreeAsync usage
- alex to check whether kernel selection code can pre-warm model shards to reduce cold allocations

ci-bot: scheduled job created: perf/staging/malloc-frag-24h (job id: 8732). will upload artifacts to /artifacts/malloc-frag/1762509999/

vlad: i'll collect the next nsys and perfetto trace after kevin's run and share a short timeline. if this fixes tail, we should consider defaulting reserve_frac to 0.8 and enable lifo reuse in the next minor release. :thumbsup:

maria: one more note — watch for CUDA memory advisor warnings in logs; they might hint at suboptimal pool alignment with device page size.

vlad: thanks all — i'll post updates here. attaching short dump of the nsys summary we used as the baseline:
```
Summary: Total cudaMalloc calls: 142, total time: 312ms, p95 single call: 18.7ms, p99 single call: 45.3ms
KV-cache churn windows aligned with malloc bursts: yes
Top caller stack: runtime/arena.cpp:alloc -> kv_cache.cpp:grow_shard -> model_loader.cpp:map_weights
```

vlad: end of thread — will follow up with artifacts.
